finding.summary: V16 currently includes credential_fingerprint in durable request identity. Rotating credential A to replacement credential B for the same admitted caller/session/client/request changes the request key. This conflicts with the owner-fixed separation between token credential and stable identity and can make cross-rotation replay recognition miss unless a higher layer compensates.
finding.important_boundary: Different request-key hashes alone prove the identity-domain split, not a duplicate external effect. Full V15/V16/effect composition must still reproduce the second admission/effect risk on target before product severity is promoted.

hypothesis.statement: Stable request/idempotency identity should bind admitted principal_id + session_ref + client_ref + request_id, while concrete credential_id/fingerprint remains separate authentication provenance and current authorization is revalidated on every attempt/replay disclosure.

strongest_counterhypothesis.statement: V16 credential-scoped request identity may be intentional if every token rotation semantically starts a new request-id namespace and clients are contractually required to mint new request IDs. No current owner-fixed contract supporting that rule was found; it would also weaken replay protection across replacement credentials for consequential operations.

proposal: Introduce stable admitted PrincipalIdentity independent of credential instance.
Represent API token as rotatable/revocable CredentialInstance linked to principal.
Derive durable RequestIdentity from principal + session + client + request_id, not credential fingerprint.
Retain credential ID/fingerprint on auth/use receipts for provenance.
Bind request identity to request semantic hash; same key with different semantics must conflict.
Revalidate current credential/principal status and scopes before replay result disclosure or any consequential action.
